clue.text: Joint game in which husband goes for runs

indicators.note: one thing going for another means it is swapped out and the other put in its place

blocks.note: a card game
H is the abbreviation for husband
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A card game where a husband dashes off to make runs, perhaps at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: In WHIST the H is replaced by R, giving WRIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrist is the hinged junction between hand and forearm, a body joint.

clue.text: Spending w/o profit by women pressing a point

indicators.note: in a down entry, pressing on something means sitting on top of it, so the earlier letters come first

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
taken as written
a stage is a point reached in a process

explanation.surface: Pointless spending by women pushing a particular argument.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'pressing' puts the W on top of what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastage is expenditure or loss that brings no benefit, spending without return.

clue.text: Reserve mob circling about Shackleton's domain?

blocks.note: ice is coolness of manner, reserve
c. is short for circa, about, used of dates circling a year
a raft is a large crowd or number

explanation.surface: A reserve crowd surrounds the subject of the explorer's realm.
explanation.walkthrough: Shackleton was an Antarctic explorer, so his realm is the skill of crossing ice; the question mark admits the definition is oblique.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice craft is skill in travelling over ice, the expertise of polar explorers like Shackleton.

clue.text: Old appearing from the get-go somewhat cutting

indicators.note: from the get-go means from the very start, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: first letter of somewhat
hewing is cutting with an axe or blade

explanation.surface: An old show seen from the outset is a bit sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' flags an archaic spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Shewing is the old spelling of showing, which means appearing.

clue.text: Indication's endorsement in X

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
an OK is approval or endorsement

explanation.surface: A sign of approval on social media platform X.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or symbol that indicates something, as in a token of thanks.

clue.text: River home to Gold Rush

indicators.note: a place that is home to something houses it, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: the Trent is a major English river
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A river that saw a gold rush, like the Klondike.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is one of England's longest rivers; 'Rush' at the end looks like part of Gold Rush but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing stream, so a rush of water or words is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Just ignoring new mass priest starts to impute any sporting site

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out of the word
starts point to the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: only and just both mean merely
N is the abbreviation for new
M is the abbreviation for mass
P is an abbreviation for priest
the first letters of impute and any

explanation.surface: A priest at mass accuses someone, with a new rule about fair play.
explanation.walkthrough: ONLY drops its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia in Greece was the site of the ancient Olympic Games, a famous sporting venue.

clue.text: Abandon agreement on damned lies

indicators.note: something damned is ruined, so these letters are wrecked and reformed

blocks.note: re means about or on
taken as written

explanation.surface: Backing out of a deal over wicked falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: To resile is to withdraw from an agreement or position, to back out of a commitment.

clue.text: Bacchante's ultimate bay and bawl?

indicators.note: ultimate means final, pointing to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the last letter of Bacchante
a voe is a bay or creek in Orkney and Shetland

explanation.surface: A frenzied follower of Bacchus finally howls and bellows.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-&lit: the Bacchante also tells you whose cry this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Evoe is the shout of joyous frenzy raised by Bacchic revellers, a ritual cry.

clue.text: Linguistic feature of addition is no longer top hell for Americans

blocks.note: nun is an obsolete word for a spinning top
nation is a US dialect euphemism for damnation

explanation.surface: Adding up is no longer the worst hell for Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' flags an obsolete sense: the top is the spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nunnation is the addition of a final n to nouns, as in Arabic declension, a grammatical feature.

clue.text: Focus of sentence slightly altering the force?

indicators.note: the focus is the centre, so the middle letters are taken
altering changes the order of the letters, slightly here as only two move

blocks.note: the central two letters of sentence
taken as written

explanation.surface: The main point of a sentence is a small change in the police?
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth is power to enforce, as when a law is said to have real teeth.

clue.text: Stop legal end of race

blocks.note: to anchor is to stop and hold fast
leg. is a dictionary abbreviation for legal

explanation.surface: A command to halt, followed by a lawful ending to a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Both parts are used in senses far from the relay meaning of the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: In a relay the anchor leg is the final stage, run by the team's last runner.

clue.text: Unlimited surge gives swing to SNP?

indicators.note: without a limit means the word's boundary letter at the end is lost

blocks.note: a sweep is a surging rush forward

explanation.surface: An unchecked wave of support produces an electoral swing to the Scottish National Party.
explanation.walkthrough: SWEEP loses its final P. The SNP is the Scottish National Party, so the question mark asks for a Scots word: swee is Scots for swing or sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Swee is a Scots verb meaning to sway or swing, the word a speaker of Scots would use.

clue.text: Naughty tyke's one that which we all turn on?

definitions.text: that which we all turn on

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and refuse to stay in their proper order

blocks.note: the possessive supplies its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mischievous child is the one who switches everything on.
explanation.walkthrough: A tyke is a cheeky child; 'turn on' here means depend on, not switch on.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central principle on which everything else depends, as an arch hangs on its wedge-shaped top stone.

clue.text: Clear up limits of tanky pile providing weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top
limits are the edges, so the outer letters are taken

blocks.note: to rid is to clear
the first and last letters of tanky
a bomb is a pile of money, a fortune

explanation.surface: Tidying the edges of a heap of tanks, which yields a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirty bomb is a conventional explosive packed with radioactive material, a weapon of terror.

clue.text: Distinguished artist inclined to lose head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word's first letter is dropped

blocks.note: Tracey Emin, the British artist
bent on something means inclined towards it

explanation.surface: A celebrated artist who is minded to be beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: BENT drops its B to become ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent and distinguished are synonyms for someone of high standing and repute.

clue.text: Short excursion could be excellent buzz

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with I for 1
to give someone a buzz is to ring them

explanation.surface: A brief outing that could give a great thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: An airing is a short walk or ride taken for fresh air, a brief outing.

clue.text: Reluctant to accept a little pot from India

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: loth is a variant spelling of loath, unwilling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hesitant to take a small Indian pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotah is a small round brass or copper water vessel used in India.

clue.text: Note level from appropriate upland

blocks.note: to appropriate something is to take it
a down is an area of open upland, as in the South Downs

explanation.surface: A musical note pitched level, drawn from a suitable hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes: take down means note in writing, take down means level a building, and the charade builds it too. Downs are English chalk hills.
explanation.definitionFit: To take down is both to write down a note and to demolish or flatten a structure.

clue.text: Gift greeting guardian of the gurdwara

blocks.note: a grant is money given
an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A present and a welcome for the keeper of a Sikh temple.
explanation.walkthrough: A gurdwara is a Sikh place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A granthi is the Sikh official who keeps and reads the holy scripture in a gurdwara.

clue.text: Blasted heavy industry, you'll possibly find it used this brass

indicators.text: you'll possibly find it used this
indicators.note: the phrase says what is left once the words it names are taken away from the fodder
blasted letters are blown apart and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Ukrainian heavy industry wrecked by war, and the money it once used.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I, T, U, S, E, D from the letters of HEAVY INDUSTRY and rearrange the rest. Brass is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The hryvnya is the currency of Ukraine, and brass is slang for money.

clue.text: Keep talking about consuming ordinary grains

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so a letter goes into the phrase

blocks.note: to harp on is to keep talking about something
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: Going on and on about eating plain cereals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grains' looks like cereal, but grains is also a forked fish spear.
explanation.definitionFit: Grains is a pronged spear for fish, so it is a kind of harpoon.

clue.text: Rumpole's pending information that is on King, aye

blocks.note: inf. is short for information
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
R is for rex, king; on means it follows
I sounds like aye, a yes vote, and stands for it in crosswords

explanation.surface: A barrister's pending case: information on the King, yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole is a fictional London barrister, so the phrase is legal Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: In fieri is a legal Latin phrase meaning in the course of being done, so still pending.

clue.text: The ear's been bent by reason of this in the past

definitions.text: by reason of this in the past

indicators.note: something bent is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's ear has been twisted for some reason long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereat is an archaic adverb meaning because of this, at this.

clue.text: Take adjective with form mostly for dish

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
a. is the abbreviation for adjective
making something is forming it

explanation.surface: A grammar instruction mixed into a recipe for a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: MAKING loses its G. Ramakin is a Chambers variant of ramekin.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramakin is a small ovenproof dish for baking and serving individual portions.

clue.text: Chap filled by that before starting to have a little port

indicators.note: starting points to the very first letter of the word that follows
a thing filled by something holds it inside

blocks.note: he stands for a man
yt is an old written abbreviation of that
the first letter of have

explanation.surface: A man packed with something before setting out to own a small harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is filled by YT followed by H.
explanation.definitionFit: A hythe is an old word for a small port or landing place, surviving in English place names.

clue.text: Jack's usual response raised every expression of surprise, say

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters run upward, so reading in reverse

blocks.note: every and all are synonyms
oh is an example of an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A sailor's typical reply was to lift up every cry of astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor, as in Jack Tar; holla is the answer to a hail of ahoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Holla is a nautical call used to reply when a ship or seaman is hailed.

clue.text: Force a cracking addendum to address

indicators.note: something cracking breaks apart, so its letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Breaking into a postscript at gunpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Care of, written c/o, is added to an address on post sent via another person.

clue.text: In the manner of a bad egg pastor dodged row

definitions.text: In the manner of a bad egg

indicators.note: the named letter dodges, slipping out of the word

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for pastor
to paddle is to row a boat, near enough

explanation.surface: A disreputable minister ducked an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: PADDLE loses its P. Bad egg suggests a rogue, but here it is a literal rotten egg.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, addle means rotten or putrid, the way a bad egg is.

clue.text: Keep an eye on obscure bottle missing name

indicators.note: missing means a letter is absent from the word that follows

blocks.note: obs. is a dictionary abbreviation for obscure
bottle is British slang for courage, or nerve
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Watch out for a murky bottle with no label.
explanation.walkthrough: NERVE loses its N. Bottle as courage is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to watch it closely, to keep an eye on it.

clue.text: African savings scheme succeeded, usually

blocks.note: s. is the abbreviation for succeeded
usu. is the dictionary abbreviation for usually

explanation.surface: A savings club in Africa generally works.
explanation.definitionFit: A susu is a rotating credit club in West Africa and the Caribbean where members pool regular savings.

clue.text: Look once and dynamic Dundee got noisier

indicators.note: something dynamic is full of motion, so these letters are moved about

blocks.note: lo is an archaic word for look
taken as written

explanation.surface: A glance back at a lively Scottish city that has grown louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks LO as an old word. Dundee is a city in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Loudened is the past tense of loudens, to become louder, so it means grew noisier.

clue.text: Percolate Scots skink with head skimmed off

indicators.note: skimming off the head removes the top, the first letter of the word

blocks.note: skink is a Scots word for drink or liquor

explanation.surface: A Scottish lizard seeps through, missing its head.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOZE loses its B. Skink looks like the lizard, but in Scots it means liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze is to seep or trickle slowly through, as liquid percolates.

clue.text: Some Puritans set off by this? It's pink and fragrant

definitions.text: Some Puritans set off by this?

blocks.clueFragment: Some Puritans set off by this?
blocks.note: first meaning: the ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620
second meaning: the trailing arbutus, a plant with fragrant pink flowers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off by' reads as triggered by, but means they sailed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Pilgrims' vessel and to several spring-blooming plants such as the trailing arbutus.

clue.text: Junction's behind American in Alabama

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the abbreviation for the state

blocks.note: the butt is the behind
A is the abbreviation for American
AL is the postal code for Alabama

explanation.surface: A road junction lies just behind an American in Alabama.
explanation.definitionFit: An abuttal is a meeting point where one property abuts another, a boundary junction.

clue.text: Going back through endless tunnel one finds lassitude

indicators.note: with no ends the word loses its letters at both extremes
going back means travelling in the opposite direction, right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Retreating through a long tunnel, someone feels weary.
explanation.walkthrough: TUNNEL trimmed at both ends leaves UNNE, which turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and boredom, a state of lassitude.
